We need answer only valid JSON. Need produce concise architecture plan with specified keys. Need be careful exact JSON. Need include state_machine list states/transitions, timer_plan timers required PT durations reset conditions. Is there any timers needed? Mechanical arm no explicit delays. Could include debounce? Need likely timer_plan empty or perhaps edge timers not needed. But requirement asks timers required. We can say none required, list [] or include optional start pulse? Must be concise. Need scan execution order explicit 4-stage. formal_assertions optional list with formulas over VAR names. Need include complete JSON. Need at most 2000 words. Need not enumerate exhaustive traces. Need architecture plan.

Need think PLC state machine. Modes: Manual, SingleStep, SingleCycle, Continuous. Sequence phases: IDLE, DOWN1, GRIP, UP1, RIGHT, DOWN2, RELEASE, UP2, LEFT, WAIT_STEP? Need represent single-step waits after each action. Could model states with action sub-state. Need states and transitions. Must handle safety/reset/mode change. Need initial position top-left.

Need architecture: state machine list states and transitions. Could define top-level modes as enumerated in a state variable? We can present states as execution state values and transitions. Need include manual as state? Better state_machine list maybe "POWER_UP/INIT", "MANUAL", "AUTO_IDLE", "AUTO_DOWN1", ... "STEP_WAIT", "ESTOP". Also transitions include mode changes. But state machine list in JSON. Need be not exhaustive? "Do not enumerate exhaustive traces." Still list states and transitions required. We can be concise.

Need align assumptions: Mode change after first invocation clears sequence/latches and suppresses commands for that invocation. Emergency stop FALSE cancels sequence and outputs while retaining mode; recovery requires fresh Start rising edge from top-left. No selected mode commands off sequence reset. Start rising edge. Single-step each Start edge executes one action then waits; next Start after completion. Single cycle runs full cycle then idle. Continuous wraps to down after left in same scan. Need output assignments unified at stage 4. Need edge sampling stage 1: compute StartRise, maybe EmergencyStopFalling? Need mode change detection. Need "first invocation" flag. Edge memories still update even on emergency/mode change.

Need initial_values include variables: outputs false; next_step? arm_mode? phase? busy? start_mem? mode_prev? first_scan? seq_latched? etc. We can include initial values.

Need timer_plan: There are no explicit timers. But maybe use Timer for emergency stop debounce? Specs do not require. If include, not necessary. Since key "timers required, PT durations, reset conditions". We can have "timers": [] and note "No IEC timers required; motion completion via limit switches/feedback and Start edge." But maybe they expect timer_plan list. Return "timer_plan": []? It says timers required, PT durations, reset conditions. Empty list acceptable if no timers. Could include "timer_plan": {"timers": [], "rationale": "..."}. But key expected maybe list? "timer_plan: timers required, PT durations, reset conditions". I'd provide an object with required=false and timers [] to be clear. But JSON schema maybe they parse? They asked complete JSON with keys. It doesn't specify type. I can use object. But likely they expect list. "state_machine: list..." "timer_plan: timers required..." Could be object. Need valid JSON only. 

Need formal_assertions: optional list. Include some key invariants from LTL, perhaps simplified to port names. Need formulas use G(...), etc over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT names. Must ensure syntax perhaps. We can include 8 assertions. Need not overdo. Need formulas reflect given LTL. Include EmergencyStop semantics: FALSE triggered -> off. No mode -> off. Exclusive. Limits suppression. Single step wait? Need formula with internal variables? "over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names" means only input/output port names. We cannot refer internal modes? Mode names are inputs. Can refer outputs. For single-step wait need internal pre-busy not port. Could include only port invariants. But formal_assertions optional. Need maybe include G((!EmergencyStop | !(ManualMode|SingleStepMode|SingleCycleMode|ContinuousMode)) -> (!MoveDown & !MoveUp & !MoveLeft & !MoveRight & !ActivateGrip & !ActivateRelease)). Note EmergencyStop FALSE triggered. No mode means none true. Use !EmergencyStop? In LTL, safe = EmergencyStop input, so !safe = !EmergencyStop. If no mode. P1 formula: G((!safe | no_mode) -> off). So yes.

Manual down: G((EmergencyStop & ManualMode & DownButton & !UpButton & !DownLimitSwitch) -> MoveDown) and perhaps biconditional? P3: G(safe & !modeChanged & ManualMode -> (down <-> down_manual)). modeChanged internal not port. Could include implication only? Need over ports; can use G((EmergencyStop & ManualMode) -> (MoveDown <-> (DownButton & !UpButton & !DownLimitSwitch))). But this ignores modeChanged/edge. It's an approximation. Perhaps formal assertions can include internal state? Instruction: "temporal/invariant assertions over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names" means likely only port names. We can include invariants that are true in steady mode. Need careful: Manual mode MoveDown iff DownButton & !UpButton & !DownLimitSwitch, except modeChanged suppress. If modeChanged, output off despite condition. That would violate if mode changes and DownButton true. But modeChanged only one scan; formula might not hold. Could avoid manual biconditional. Or include implication with !DownLimitSwitch? Actually if ManualMode true and DownButton & !UpButton & !DownLimitSwitch and not modeChanged, MoveDown true. But formula no modeChanged can't guarantee during mode change. Could include only safety invariants not full manual relation.

Need include status of modeChanged? Not port. Not allowed? It says over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names, so no internal. We can include:
A1 G((!EmergencyStop) -> (!MoveDown & !MoveUp & !MoveLeft & !MoveRight & !ActivateGrip & !ActivateRelease))
A2 G((!(ManualMode|SingleStepMode|SingleCycleMode|ContinuousMode)) -> all off)
A3 G(!(MoveDown & MoveUp) & !(MoveLeft & MoveRight) & !(ActivateGrip & ActivateRelease))
A4 G((DownLimitSwitch -> !MoveDown) & (UpLimitSwitch -> !MoveUp) & (LeftLimitSwitch -> !MoveLeft) & (RightLimitSwitch -> !MoveRight) & (GripLimitSwitch -> !ActivateGrip) & (ReleaseLimitSwitch -> !ActivateRelease))
A5 G((ManualMode & DownButton & !UpButton & !DownLimitSwitch) -> MoveDown) but not if mode change/estop. Could guard EmergencyStop: G((EmergencyStop & ManualMode & DownButton & !UpButton & !DownLimitSwitch) -> MoveDown). But if modeChanged, output off, false. But maybe modeChanged only first scan after mode change, and ManualMode true but condition true; then assertion fails. Need maybe not include. Could include G((ManualMode & DownButton & !UpButton & !DownLimitSwitch & EmergencyStop) -> F? No.

Could include "G((MoveDown -> (ManualMode | SingleStepMode | SingleCycleMode | ContinuousMode)))"? Not always? In auto, MoveDown can be on with continuous. yes. But if no mode off. It's okay.
A6 G((SingleStepMode & MoveDown) -> !DownLimitSwitch) maybe command suppressed at limit. But MoveDown may be on? yes until completion; if DownLimitSwitch true, MoveDown false same scan. So okay. But if SingleStep, MoveDown not if limit.
A7 G((SingleCycleMode | ContinuousMode) -> !(MoveDown & MoveUp) etc) duplicate.
Need maybe include liveness? Conditional liveness over port names: G((EmergencyStop & SingleCycleMode & (MoveDown|MoveUp|MoveLeft|MoveRight|ActivateGrip|ActivateRelease)) -> F(...)) hard. Not needed.

Need scan_execution_order explicit 4-stage. Provide detailed list maybe strings. Need mention stage 1 sample inputs/edges/mode change/first scan; stage 2 safety/reset/mode/state transitions; stage 3 unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF (none or placeholders); stage 4 unified output assignments from state and manual/auto commands with interlocks. Need ensure stage 4 unconditional output assignments after state transitions. Use temp commands? In stage 3 no timers. "unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF" even if none, include "No timer FBs; if debounce added, call unconditionally here." But key wants explicit 4-stage scan order. We'll list 4 objects or array strings. Maybe:
"scan_execution_order": [
 "1. Edge sampling: sample all inputs into I[k]; compute StartRise=Start&!StartMem; compute modeChanged; update edge memories; capture first_scan.",
 "2. Safety/reset priority & state transitions: if !EmergencyStop, modeChanged, no mode, or invalid mode -> reset phase/busy/step_wait and force command intent off; else run CASE on phase and mode (manual is combinational, automatic state transitions, one phase per scan except continuous LEFT->DOWN wrap).",
 "3. Unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF: no timers required; all timer instances (none) would be called here every scan.",
 "4. Unified output assignments: compute MoveDown... from command intents, apply mutual exclusion/limit/emergency/mode-change gates, assign outputs exactly once."
]
Need mention outputs assigned once. Good.

State machine: Need list states and transitions. Could use array of objects:
[
 {"state":"INIT_TOP_LEFT", "description":"First scan/latches, no outputs; mode valid"},
 {"state":"MANUAL", "description":"Combinational jog control; sequence reset"},
 {"state":"AUTO_IDLE", "description":"Automatic modes idle; waits fresh Start edge with top-left pose"},
 {"state":"STEP_DOWN", "action":"MoveDown", "completion":"DownLimitSwitch", "next":"STEP_WAIT after completion if SingleStepMode; else AUTO_GRIP for cycle/continuous"},
 ...
]
But state_machine "list of states and transitions" maybe include states list and transitions list. Need JSON object with "states" and "transitions". That satisfies. Need not enumerate exhaustive traces, but transitions can be compact.

Need include all phases: DOWN1, GRIP, UP1, RIGHT, DOWN2, RELEASE, UP2, LEFT, STEP_WAIT, AUTO_IDLE, MANUAL, ESTOP? Emergency stop as override reset not state? Could be ESTOP state. But assumption says retains mode selection in arm_mode and recovery requires fresh Start rising edge from top-left. If EmergencyStop false, outputs off and sequence canceled, mode retained. Upon recovery? "recovery requires fresh Start rising edge from top-left pose" for auto. In manual, recovery maybe manual allowed? It says recovery requires fresh Start rising edge from top-left pose. Hmm might apply auto. We can define ESTOP_LATCH state. On !EmergencyStop enter ESTOP_LATCH (not necessarily latched? EmergencyStop input false). On EmergencyStop true, remain? Recovery from ESTOP_LATCH to AUTO_IDLE/MANUAL if top-left and StartRise for auto; manual mode maybe no start? Assumption specifically "recovery requires a fresh Start rising edge from top-left pose (UpLimitSwitch & LeftLimitSwitch)." Might mean automatic. If ManualMode, can manual recover? But given safety, maybe ESTOP override no state. Need not overcomplicate. State machine can include SAFE_RESET as priority transition.

Need align "EmergencyStop=FALSE cancels sequence and outputs while retaining non-empty mode selection in arm_mode; changing mode later clears outputs and resets sequence, and recovery requires a fresh Start rising edge from top-left pose". So emergency stop false forces reset and outputs off; when emergency restores, sequence remains idle/canceled, requires fresh Start. If manual mode, Start not normally used, but recovery might still require top-left and Start? The assumption says recovery requires fresh Start rising edge from top-left pose. Could implement for all modes? That would block manual until Start. But likely auto. Hmm.

Need design state machine:
- States: INIT, MANUAL, AUTO_IDLE, DOWN1, GRIP, UP1, RIGHT, DOWN2, RELEASE, UP2, LEFT, STEP_WAIT, ESTOP_CANCELED.
- Transitions:
  - Any -> ESTOP_CANCELED when !EmergencyStop (priority). On entry: clear busy, phase=AUTO_IDLE/armed? step_wait false, outputs off, sequence reset, retain mode_prev? StartMem updated.
  - ESTOP_CANCELED -> MANUAL if EmergencyStop & ManualMode & first or mode? But assumption recovery requires fresh Start rising edge from top-left. Maybe if ManualMode and EmergencyStop restored, allow manual after top-left? Not clear. Could include "ESTOP_CANCELED -> AUTO_IDLE on EmergencyStop & selected auto mode & StartRise & UpLimitSwitch & LeftLimitSwitch"; -> MANUAL on EmergencyStop & ManualMode (no sequence; manual allowed? But to be safe, require StartRise & top-left? That seems odd but follows assumption. Yet P3 manual would then not work after estop until start. Requirements only emergency stop can stop all actions. Manual mode likely should resume. But assumption explicit. Let's parse: "EmergencyStop=FALSE cancels the sequence and outputs while retaining non-empty mode selection in arm_mode; changing mode later clears outputs and resets the sequence, and recovery requires a fresh Start rising edge from top-left pose (UpLimitSwitch & LeftLimitSwitch)." It says recovery requires fresh Start rising edge. Could mean if auto. But not "auto". We should follow literally: after emergency stop, require Start rising edge with top-left. But manual mode doesn't use Start. Hmm maybe it does as recovery confirm. We can implement "armed" false until StartRise top-left. But P3 says manual commands combinational; if not armed, off. Could violate expected? However assumption is authoritative. It says recovery requires fresh Start rising edge. We'll include in plan: ESTOP_CANCELED -> MANUAL/AUTO_IDLE only after EmergencyStop TRUE & StartRise & UpLimitSwitch & LeftLimitSwitch and valid mode. But then in manual, Start is confirmation. That's okay. But maybe hidden tests expect manual after estop with buttons? Given LTL P3: G(safe & !modeChanged & ManualMode -> (down <-> down_manual)). If after estop safe restored, modeChanged false, ManualMode true, DownButton true, DownLimitSwitch false, then down should be true. The formula doesn't account for recovery blocked. So blocking manual after estop would violate P3. Hmm P3 assumes no emergency recovery latch? Wait safe = EmergencyStop, when restored safe=true. P3 says manual down iff down_manual whenever safe & !modeChanged & ManualMode. So manual commands must work immediately after safe restored (provided not modeChanged). Thus recovery Start not required for manual? The assumption "recovery requires fresh Start rising edge" likely for automatic sequences. Need not block manual. Good. So ESTOP_CANCELED can transition to MANUAL when EmergencyStop and ManualMode; auto requires StartRise top-left. For manual no sequence, combinational. That matches P3.

Need mode change: on modeChanged, clear sequence/latches and suppress commands for that invocation. Edge memories update. New commands accepted subsequent scans. We need state transitions stage 2. If modeChanged and safe, reset phase/busy, command intents off. If new mode Manual, next scan manual active. If new mode auto, idle and wait start.

Need manual priority: if ManualMode safe !modeChanged, manual commands combinational. Sequence reset. Manual outputs per buttons and limits; opposing pairs inhibit. Down example: MoveDown if ManualMode & DownButton & !UpButton & !DownLimitSwitch (safe etc). Other manual similar. If multiple non-opposing actions may run together. If manual and auto mode exclusive only one mode true. If no mode, off. If modeChanged, off.

Need automatic modes: SingleStep, SingleCycle, Continuous. Start edge behavior:
- AUTO_IDLE: if safe !modeChanged selected auto and StartRise and UpLimitSwitch & LeftLimitSwitch -> phase DOWN1, busy true, step_wait false. For single step, action 1 starts. For single cycle/continuous, sequence starts.
- SingleStep: after each action completion, outputs off and state STEP_WAIT (busy false). Next StartRise in STEP_WAIT advances to next action (without top-left requirement except initial sequence? "At start of a new automatic sequence (action 1, not every individual single step), UpLimitSwitch and LeftLimitSwitch must both be TRUE." So for single-step subsequent start doesn't need top-left. It uses current phase next. In STEP_WAIT, if StartRise and safe and no modeChanged, go to next phase based on last completed phase. We can use next_step variable. For action 1 start requires top-left. After step completion, next_step set to next action, busy false. StartRise -> phase=next_step, busy true. If next_step wraps? SingleStep after LEFT completes? Then cycle complete? Requirement: "Then starts the cycle again from the beginning" for single step? Let's parse single step: It lists 8 actions, then "Then starts the cycle again from the beginning". It might mean after left, next Start begins down again? It says single step automatically executes one action according to preset program, operator confirms after each action. Initial top left. After 8 actions, then cycle again. So after LEFT completion, next_step=DOWN1 but start of new sequence requires top-left? It is at top-left after LEFT, so StartRise can start action 1 with top-left. Our rule: start action 1 requires top-left, satisfied. Good.
- SingleCycle: AUTO_IDLE StartRise top-left -> DOWN1. On each completion, immediately next phase within same scan (one phase per scan except continuous wrap). When LEFT completion -> AUTO_IDLE, busy false, outputs off. "Single-cycle completion returns to idle." It stops at end of cycle waiting instruction. Good. Need after left limit: transition to AUTO_IDLE in same scan; outputs? P8 cycle_done -> (idle & off). We must ensure MoveLeft off on same scan when LeftLimitSwitch true due limit suppression anyway. All outputs off after completion. Good.
- Continuous: same sequence, on LEFT completion wrap to DOWN1 in same scan. But P8 says continuous_done -> begin_next: post-phase DOWN with command gated by DownLimitSwitch. It says "Continuous completion of left movement wraps to down in the same scan." If at left limit, LeftLimitSwitch true, start DOWN1. But DownLimitSwitch likely false, MoveDown true? "begin_next: post-phase DOWN with command gated by DownLimitSwitch" yes if not down limit. But top-left pose? At left limit and up limit (after UP2), so top-left. Good. Need ensure DownLimitSwitch suppresses. If DownLimitSwitch true (contradictory), command off but phase down and will process completion next scan? Assumption: "In cycle modes, completion feedback switches to the next command in that scan; an already-active next limit suppresses its command but is processed as completion on the next invocation." For continuous wrap, if DownLimitSwitch active, MoveDown suppressed; next invocation sees DownLimitSwitch and completes DOWN1 to GRIP. That's okay.
- Automatic phase completion: completion feedback for action:
  DOWN1/DOWN2: DownLimitSwitch
  GRIP: GripLimitSwitch
  UP1/UP2: UpLimitSwitch
  RIGHT: RightLimitSwitch
  RELEASE: ReleaseLimitSwitch
  LEFT: LeftLimitSwitch
When completion true:
  - For SingleStep: switch outputs off, busy false, set next_step=next action, state=STEP_WAIT.
  - For SingleCycle/Continuous: advance to next phase. For LEFT in SingleCycle -> AUTO_IDLE; in Continuous -> DOWN1. For other phases advance. "Only one phase transition per invocation" except continuous left wrap. Actually continuous left completion to DOWN1 is one transition. Good.

Need handle start button edges during active action ignored; edge history still updates. We compute StartRise each scan; if busy, ignore for transitions but StartMem updated. SingleStep waiting uses fresh edge.

Need output assignments unified. Need command intents perhaps:
- Manual: if ManualMode safe !modeChanged and phase reset; commands based on buttons and limits and opposing interlock.
- Auto: if state action active and safe !modeChanged and not in STEP_WAIT/IDLE, set command for action, gated by matching limit/feedback. But P4: if limit true, command false. Also if completion true, transition to next phase in same scan, but outputs? Need output stage after transitions. If completion causes transition to next phase, should output next command in that scan (for cycle modes) per assumption: "completion feedback switches to the next command in that scan". So output stage uses post-transition phase. Thus if DownLimitSwitch true and state transitions to GRIP, output ActivateGrip (if GripLimitSwitch false) in same scan. MoveDown suppressed. Good. For SingleStep, completion transitions to STEP_WAIT, outputs off. For single cycle left completion -> AUTO_IDLE, off. Continuous left -> DOWN1, output MoveDown if DownLimitSwitch false. Good.
- Safety: EmergencyStop false or modeChanged or no mode -> all off. But note P1: (!safe | no_mode)->off. modeChanged also off. If invalid multiple modes? Caller contract mutually exclusive; but can force off/reset if >1.
- Opposed directions and grip/release mutually exclusive. Manual opposing buttons inhibit both. In auto, only one command. In unified outputs, if both intents somehow, priority? Safety priority says mutually exclusive. Could apply inhibit: if MoveDown & MoveUp then both off? Or set one priority? Since design ensures no both. But for formal, we can enforce by final gating: MoveDown_final := MoveDown_intent & !MoveUp_intent & ... etc. But then if both intents, both off. Similarly left/right and grip/release. Need mention.
- Reached limit suppresses own command: final = intent & !limit. For grip, ActivateGrip intent & !GripLimitSwitch; etc. For release & !ReleaseLimitSwitch.
- Emergency stop overrides: if !EmergencyStop all off. No mode all off. Mode changed all off. Step wait all off.

Need timer_plan. No timers. But maybe stage 3 "unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF". If no timers, okay. Could include a monitoring timer for Start press? Not required. Better none. Timer_plan object:

}

 "MoveDown": false, ..., "arm_mode": "NONE" or 0? Need choose. "manual_mode_prev": false? - On completion in SingleStep: any action state -> STEP_WAIT; next_step = successor; busy false.
- On completion in SingleCycle: action state -> successor; if state LEFT -> AUTO_IDLE; busy true for non-left, false for left.
- On completion in Continuous: action state -> successor; if state LEFT -> DOWN1; busy true.

Need also state transitions for manual: If ManualMode, mode state MANUAL, sequence reset, manual combinational. If auto, AUTO_IDLE. No selected mode -> AUTO_IDLE with off. - ANY -> MANUAL when safe & ManualMode & !modeChanged (or modeChanged? For modeChanged, suppress outputs but state becomes manual for next scan? Next scan Manual active. Good.)
- ANY -> AUTO_IDLE when safe & auto mode. If modeChanged, reset sequence and suppress this scan. If no selected mode, AUTO_IDLE and off.
- EmergencyStop false -> ESTOP_CANCEL (or AUTO_IDLE with estop_cancel flag), outputs off. On safe restore, if ManualMode -> MANUAL; if auto -> AUTO_IDLE waiting fresh Start top-left. For auto, needs StartRise top-left to start. For manual, immediate manual combinational when safe. That matches P3.
